subject: Copywriting
title: The Propaganda Techniques Checklist
description: Learn The Propaganda Techniques Checklist in one minute.

hook.text: In 1938, the Institute for Propaganda Analysis published 7 common techniques.

buildup.text: The seven: Name Calling, Glittering Generalities, Transfer, Testimonial, Plain Folks, Card Stacking, and Bandwagon.

discovery.text: 'Plain Folks' shows a billionaire eating at a diner. 'Transfer' wraps a product in a flag.

twist.text: Modern propaganda blends multiple techniques in a single message.

climax.text: The checklist turns invisible manipulation visible. Once you see the technique, the spell weakens.

punchline.text: Seven techniques from 1938. They still decode almost all propaganda.

quiz.question: How many techniques did the 1938 Institute for Propaganda Analysis identify?

details.whyItMatters: Having a checklist of propaganda techniques creates a practical framework for analyzing any persuasive message. These seven patterns appear in virtually every propaganda campaign ever created.
takeaways: Seven classic techniques cover most propaganda strategies
Name-calling and glittering generalities manipulate through language
Bandwagon and testimonial exploit social proof and authority

faq.question: What are the seven propaganda techniques?
faq.answer: Name-calling (negative labels), glittering generalities (vague positive terms), transfer (associating with respected symbols), testimonial (celebrity endorsement), plain folks (appearing ordinary), card stacking (selective evidence), and bandwagon (everyone is doing it).

faq.question: Are these techniques still relevant today?
faq.answer: Extremely. Every political campaign, advertising blitz, and social media influence operation uses some combination of these seven techniques. The medium changes — from pamphlets to TikTok — but the psychological mechanisms they exploit remain constant.
